title: Accelerating Discovery in Natural Science Laboratories with AI and Robotics: Perspectives and Challenges from the 2024 IEEE ICRA Workshop, Yokohama, Japan

metadata.authors: A. I. Cooper; P. Courtney; K. Darvish; M. Eckhoff; H. Fakhruldeen; A. Gabrielli; A. Garg; S. Haddadin; K. Harada; J. Hein; M. Hübner; D. Knobbe; G. Pizzuto; F. Shkurti; R. Shrestha; K. Thurow; R. Vescovi; B. Vogel-Heuser; Á Wolf; N. Yoshikawa; Y. Zeng; Z. Zhou; H. Zwirnmann

source_summary: Science laboratory automation accelerates discovery in life sciences and materials but faces challenges—including autonomy, reproducibility, throughput, standardization, human roles, and ethics—that require interdisciplinary collaboration, as discussed by leading experts in this article.
abstract: Science laboratory automation enables accelerated discovery in life sciences and materials. However, it requires interdisciplinary collaboration to address challenges such as robust and flexible autonomy, reproducibility, throughput, standardization, the role of human scientists, and ethics. This article highlights these issues, reflecting perspectives from leading experts in laboratory automation across different disciplines of the natural sciences.

methods.value: The method involves a workshop facilitating knowledge exchange between academic researchers and industry partners, featuring experts in robotics and professionals from various industries, to discuss and identify challenges and solutions in science lab automation.

problems.value: The core scientific problem is the challenge of automating natural science laboratories to accelerate discovery, which requires addressing issues like robust and flexible autonomy, reproducibility, throughput, standardization, the role of human scientists, and ethics.

hypotheses.value: The hypothesis is that interdisciplinary collaboration and advancements in AI and robotics can effectively address these challenges and fundamentally accelerate knowledge generation and discovery in semi-structured environments across the natural sciences.

evidence.value: The evidence includes perspectives from leading experts in laboratory automation across different disciplines of the natural sciences, as well as insights from recent works and pioneering efforts in the field.

conclusions.value: The paper concludes that science lab automation has the potential to transform research across disciplines by making experimentation more precise, efficient, and reproducible, but achieving this vision requires overcoming challenges in integrating diverse instruments, managing vast data through AI-driven insights, fostering industry collaboration for standardization, and carefully addressing ethical concerns.
